interpretation: The validated V8 calculation produced an overall percentage of 68.8%.

causal_findings.summary: The heading mixes political crisis, institutional reform, popular action, diplomacy, war, and retrospective discussion across the whole work. Chronological phases and thematic subheads for institutions, popular action, foreign affairs, and later interpretation would provide useful entry points. Fifty-three displayed locators, including several long ranges, force the reader to scan a book-spanning string for unrelated treatments. The proposed divisions are substantive historical topics, not cosmetic buckets.

The heading combines constitutional settlement, flight and monarchical crisis, church conflict, war preparations, and later references to the year. Subheads for the constitutional settlement, royal crisis, religious conflict, and foreign affairs would expose the distinct treatments. Twenty-eight displays include a sixty-one-page range and do not let readers identify the relevant 1791 topic without page-by-page inspection. The divisions correspond to independent historical subjects.
The supported year treatment requires thematic subdivisions for distinct political, military, religious, and economic developments.
The supported year treatment requires thematic subdivisions for distinct political, military, religious, and economic developments.
The supported year treatment requires thematic subdivisions for distinct constitutional, political, economic, religious, and diplomatic developments.
The delivered access label Amadeus, Victor inverts or fragments the familiar personal name established by the registered source evidence, slowing alphabetical lookup under the expected name form.
Unlinked synonymous headings split substantively related access across distant alphabetic routes.
Readers using either standard term receive only part of the political-order treatment.
The source identity is Marie Antoinette, but the delivered access form treats Antoinette as a surname. The personal name is inverted as Antoinette, Marie rather than filed as Marie Antoinette.

The references separate diplomatic bargaining and alliances from campaigns, occupation, and military confrontation across several periods. Split the entry into at least diplomacy and war, with chronological or campaign subheads where useful. Seventeen displays force readers seeking one of the two express facets to scan the other facet across nineteen assignments. The compound heading joins two durable concepts whose separation would materially improve retrieval.
The full-name route contains only a small fragment of the treatment placed under the surname-only route.
The full-name route contains only a small fragment of the treatment placed under the surname-only route.

The Bordeaux string combines prerevolutionary institutions, municipal politics, unrest, federalism, war, trade, and later regime changes. Subheads for local institutions, popular politics, federalism, economic life, and later revolutionary phases would provide useful access. Thirty displayed locators scattered across the work make a topic-specific Bordeaux reference difficult to locate. The proposed groupings are independent historical treatments.
Twenty-four displays span distinct institutional, political, religious, and counter-revolutionary regional treatments.
The source identity is Maria Carolina, but the delivered access form treats Carolina as a surname. The royal given names are inverted as Carolina, Maria rather than Maria Carolina.
A reader using either plausible personal-name form sees only part of the person's treatment.
A reader using either plausible personal-name form sees only part of the person's treatment.

The heading combines Catholic belief, clergy and institutions, lay communities, confessional conflict, and political alignment. Use separate routes such as Catholic Church and clergy, Catholic laity, confessional conflict, and political Catholicism. Twenty-seven displays and thirty-four assignments under an adjectival heading make a reader scan unrelated religious and political facets. The distinctions are durable subject concepts, not trivial chronology.
The route should use the complete institutional name or link explicitly to National Constituent Assembly.

The references treat the Crown as executive authority, fiscal actor, dynastic institution, and political symbol. Subdivide by executive/governmental authority, finance, dynasty, and symbolic legitimacy. Nineteen displays make readers disentangle several institutional senses of Crown. The distinctions are conceptual roles rather than trivial page groupings.

The delivered access label Côte d’Or, Prieur de inverts or fragments the familiar personal name established by the registered source evidence, slowing alphabetical lookup under the expected name form.

The heading aggregates many countries, alliances, wars, diplomatic systems, political reactions, and retrospective continental comparisons. Subheads by region and by diplomacy, warfare, political influence, and international reaction would supply useful access. Thirty-eight displays with several very long ranges make a specific European treatment impossible to identify efficiently. The divisions are independent geographic and international subjects.
Domestic institutions, society, economy, religion, war, diplomacy, expansion, and legacy require separate access routes.
The heading refers to Francis II, but the regnal numeral is incorrectly treated as an inverted surname. II, Francis is an invalid regnal-name inversion; Francis II is the usable form.

The references separate Jacobin control of institutions, policies, factional struggles, and distinct phases of political power. Subdivide by institutional control, policy, factional conflict, and chronological phase. Twenty-nine displays and thirty-three assignments make the reader scan different forms and periods of Jacobin power. These are durable political facets, not trivial page clusters.
The bare adjective obscures whether a destination concerns an assembly, guard, property, sovereignty, policy, religion, or identity.
Complete noun phrases and concept-specific routes are required to replace the undifferentiated adjective string.
The path asserts National Guard activity outside France, but the audited destinations overwhelmingly concern forces within France or amalgamation into the army.
The delivered access label Nemours, dupont de inverts or fragments the familiar personal name established by the registered source evidence, slowing alphabetical lookup under the expected name form.
The post-Napoleonic-kingdom qualifier is absent from most destinations assigned to the path.
Unlinked synonymous headings split substantively related access across distant alphabetic routes.
Readers using either standard term receive only part of the political-order treatment.

The heading combines armed resistance, political opposition, religious resistance, local/community action, and resistance to policy across many settings. Subdivide by armed, political, religious, and local resistance, with named movements or regions as routes. Fifty-four displays and seventy-two assignments under a generic heading impose substantial scanning across unrelated forms of resistance. The forms of resistance are durable concepts, not page-count artifacts.
The complete path presents Russia as revolutionary although all audited destinations describe monarchy, anti-revolution, coalition politics, or unrealized hopes.

The references treat State authority through law, administration, coercion, finance, sovereignty, and relations with local institutions. Subdivide by legal/administrative authority, coercive authority, fiscal authority, and sovereignty or central-local relations. Twenty singleton displays under an abstract heading require readers to distinguish several functions without guidance. The functions are substantive state roles.
The delivered access label Theresia, Maria inverts or fragments the familiar personal name established by the registered source evidence, slowing alphabetical lookup under the expected name form.
The heading refers to William V, but the regnal numeral is incorrectly treated as an inverted surname. V, William is an invalid regnal-name inversion; William V is the usable form.
Twenty-seven displays cover several distinct institutional and event functions of the place.
The complete path asserts a palace relationship that none of its audited destinations supports.
The path labels armies as insurgents, while most destinations concern regular, coalition, or revolutionary armies rather than insurgent forces.

royal, legislative, executive, judicial, popular, and military authority during revolution. Useful routes: authority—royal; legislative; executive; judicial; popular; military. Consequence: forty-five displayed locators force scanning across unrelated kinds of authority.
The path conflates the legal-profession sense of bar with a physical barrier; none of its audited destinations supports the asserted sense.
Unlinked synonymous headings split substantively related access across distant alphabetic routes.

The generic heading combines named political clubs, local societies, literary or social associations, organizational activity, repression, and later revival. Subheads by named organization and by political, local, social, and repressive functions would create useful routes. Twenty-five displays scattered across the chronology make the intended kind of club hard to locate. The divisions represent distinct institutions and functions.
The generic noun omits the institutional identity necessary to interpret each destination.
Named-body or function-based routes are required for the thirty-three-display string.

The references separate constitutional design, rights, governmental organization, revision, and the use of constitutions across successive regimes. Subdivide by constitutional design and rights, governmental organization, and named constitutional settlements or periods. Nineteen displays and twenty-two assignments make a reader scan distinct constitutional functions. The proposed facets are durable concepts and materially improve retrieval.
The path mixes the princely-household sense of court with judicial courts; most destinations support the latter sense instead.
The heading names the royal heir rather than Dauphiné, so the province is represented as the wrong referent. Dropping the final e and accent changes Dauphiné into dauphin and misfiles the province.
The delivered access label de Fleury, Joly inverts or fragments the familiar personal name established by the registered source evidence, slowing alphabetical lookup under the expected name form.
The heading refers to Rouget de Lisle, but the filing form moves the particle and given element into a false surname inversion. de Lisle, Rouget misfiles the established name Rouget de Lisle.
The path conflates territorial departments with government ministries and has no supported destination.

deputies by assembly, faction, mission, social origin, and parliamentary action. Useful routes: deputies—Estates-General; Legislative Assembly; Convention; on mission; factions. Consequence: fifty-four displayed locators and a long range obstruct targeted retrieval by role or body.

The generic heading combines feudal, seigneurial, ecclesiastical, fiscal, and commercial dues in different institutional settings. Subheads by feudal, church, state, and commercial obligations would provide useful access. Eleven displays and sixteen assignments require readers to infer which kind of due each page treats. The proposed groups are distinct legal and fiscal concepts.

The references concern executions of different people, judicial executions, political reprisals, and wartime or mass violence. Subdivide by named defendant or victim, judicial execution, and collective or wartime execution. Twenty displays require readers to identify unrelated executions from undifferentiated page references. The distinctions are independent events and legal contexts.

The heading mixes voluntary and forced exile, émigré politics, deportation, refuge, individual flight, and returns under different regimes. Subheads for émigrés, deportation, political refuge, individual exile, and return would be useful. Twenty-two displays scattered across the chronology materially slow retrieval of a particular kind of exile. These are distinct legal and political forms of displacement.
The historiography qualifier is not supported by any audited destination on the path.
Unlinked synonymous headings split substantively related access across distant alphabetic routes.
Unlinked synonymous headings split substantively related access across distant alphabetic routes.

The references distinguish constitutional sovereignty, royal prerogative, sacral or symbolic sovereignty, and conflicts over the king's authority. Subdivide by constitutional sovereignty, prerogative, symbolism, and conflicts over authority. Twenty-nine displays and thirty-seven assignments obscure which sense of sovereignty a page treats. The distinctions are separate institutional and symbolic roles.

The references cover executive decision-making, ministers, legislative relations, vetoes, and crises of royal government. Subdivide by executive authority, ministers, relations with assemblies, and governmental crisis. Twenty-six displays make readers scan several functions of the king in government. The proposed facets represent distinct governmental relationships.

The references mix restoration projects, claimants, diplomacy, public expectations, and actual postrevolutionary settlements. Subdivide by restoration plans and claimants, foreign diplomacy, public royalism, and realized restoration. Thirty-four displays and thirty-nine assignments obscure distinct restoration contexts. The distinctions are substantive routes, even after locator mismatches are kept separate.

The heading combines legislation, courts, criminal law, constitutional law, administrative law, social regulation, property law, and named enactments. Subheads by legal domain and named law, with routes for legislative process and judicial institutions, would materially improve access. Seventy displayed locators across the work make a particular legal topic extremely difficult to retrieve. The divisions are established legal concepts rather than arbitrary page groups.

constitutional, penal, economic, religious, and emergency revolutionary laws. Useful routes: laws—constitutional; penal; economic; religious; emergency. Consequence: thirty displays mix distinct legal subjects and slow any issue-specific lookup.
Seventeen displays cover distinct governmental functions that should be separately named.
Distinct officeholding, judicial, resistance, and public-order treatments remain in one long locator string.
The bare word does not identify whether the route concerns liturgy, mobilization, demonstrations, or merely a large-scale modifier.
The long string requires concept-complete routes for liturgy, mobilization, and other distinct senses.

The generic heading combines September killings, battlefield or prison massacres, local reprisals, colonial violence, and later retrospective references. Subheads by named massacre, location, and political or military context would provide useful access. Thirteen unqualified page references make readers inspect every destination to find the intended massacre. Named events and contexts are substantive distinctions.

the Maximum as price-control law versus wages, enforcement, and variant duplicate headings. Useful routes: Maximum—law and adoption; enforcement; wage controls, with variant headings consolidated. Consequence: fifteen displays plus duplicate access terms fragment a single policy and slow retrieval.

The references concern different ministers, portfolios, policy domains, and phases of revolutionary government. Subdivide by portfolio or minister and by major governmental phase. Twenty-two displays and twenty-nine assignments force readers to scan unrelated offices and policy contexts. Ministerial office and governmental phase are durable conceptual distinctions.

The references distinguish finance, foreign affairs, justice, household, and other royal ministerial functions across changing ministries. Subdivide by portfolio or named ministry, with chronological grouping where needed. Seventeen displays and twenty-one assignments obscure which royal governmental function is treated. The divisions are substantive offices rather than trivial chronology.
The path conflates ministry as a government department with cabinet or ministerial contexts and has no supported destination.

The entry explicitly combines abolition of monarchy with later restoration projects and settlements, along with the intervening debate over monarchical survival. Separate abolition, restoration projects, and restored monarchy, with chronological qualification. Twenty-seven displays and thirty-three assignments make opposite political processes share one undifferentiated string. Abolition and restoration are distinct, nontrivial concepts.
The path reverses the source relation: national or Church property is put at the nation’s disposal; the nation is not property. No independent mechanics defect beyond the semantic heading error.

The references concern allegiance by clergy, officials, soldiers, and citizens to different constitutional or political authorities. Subdivide by oath-taking group and by regime or authority receiving allegiance. Fourteen displays and sixteen assignments obscure whose allegiance and which authority each page concerns. The actors and political objects are distinct conceptual relationships.
Unlinked synonymous headings split substantively related access across distant alphabetic routes.

The references concern different monastic orders, their property, suppression, charity, and political-religious status. Subdivide by named order and by property/suppression, charity, and political status. Twenty-four displays and twenty-six assignments require scanning across different institutions and functions. The distinctions are durable monastic subjects, even though many individual locator failures remain separate.

The path combines municipal government, popular action, sections, clubs, court and Assembly politics, economy, policing, violence, culture, and later regimes in Paris. Subheads for municipal government, popular movements, institutions, economy, violence, political venues, and chronological phases would create high-value routes. Ninety-seven displays and 186 assignments create an exceptionally burdensome string in which a specific Paris topic cannot be located efficiently. The proposed divisions are major urban, institutional, and chronological subjects.

The references distinguish judicial jurisdiction, registration and remonstrance, institutional reform, political opposition, personnel, and public conflict around the Parlement of Paris. Subdivide by jurisdiction and judicial role, registration/remonstrance, reform and suppression, and political/public conflict. Seventeen displays expand to thirty-six assignments and conceal several institutional functions behind one string. The functions are nontrivial access concepts and the locator failures remain separately recorded.

The references use patriots for different regional groups, political alignments, and phases of revolutionary activity within France. Subdivide by region or political grouping and by major phase where identities change. Twenty-one displays and twenty-four assignments make the broad collective label difficult to navigate. Regional and political identities are durable distinctions.

people as sovereign, crowd, social category, nation, and rhetorical collective. Useful routes: people—popular sovereignty; urban crowd; social groups; political rhetoric. Consequence: seventy-nine displayed locators force readers across unrelated meanings of people.
The path mixes the noun 'poor' with incidental adjectival uses of 'inadequate'; most destinations do not treat poor people as inadequate.
Unlinked synonymous headings split substantively related access across distant alphabetic routes.

The references distinguish legal persecution, violence, deportation, dechristianization, and regionally different treatment of priests. Subdivide by legal measures, violence/deportation, dechristianization, and region or period. Twenty-nine displays and thirty-four assignments obscure distinct forms and settings of persecution. The distinctions are substantive mechanisms and contexts, not trivial chronology.
The sole destination does not treat progress as an idea, leaving the access route unsupported.

The generic heading combines institutional purges, factional removals, electoral exclusions, military or administrative dismissals, and post-Thermidor reactions. Subheads by institution, faction, regime, and type of removal would give readers useful routes. Nineteen displays scattered across the work make a particular purge difficult to identify. The distinctions are independent political processes, not arbitrary page groups.

The references distinguish the queen's court networks, foreign contacts, flight and plots, propaganda image, and role in counter-revolutionary strategy. Subdivide by court networks, foreign relations, flight/plots, and political representation. Twenty displays and twenty-eight assignments make distinct counter-revolutionary roles difficult to locate. These are substantive modes of action and representation.

The heading aggregates different radical factions, local activists, ideological positions, and successive revolutionary periods. Subheads by faction, locality, ideology, and period would provide meaningful access. Fifteen displays offer no clue which radical group or episode each destination treats. The divisions are distinct actors and political currents.
The heading merges the Cult or concept of Reason with ordinary connective uses of the word. The defect is semantic selection, not typography.

The references mix institutions, violence, political factions, policy, regional events, and social responses during the Terror. Subdivide by institutions/policy, repression and violence, factions, and regional experience. Forty displays and sixty assignments make the broad temporal heading difficult to use for any one facet. The distinctions are substantive aspects of revolution during the Terror.

The references distinguish diffusion of revolutionary ideas, wars, occupations, national movements, and political settlements across many European countries. Subdivide by diffusion/ideas, war and occupation, national movements, and geographic region or country. Thirty-nine displays and fifty-nine assignments obscure different mechanisms and locations of revolution in Europe. The proposed routes are major conceptual and geographic distinctions.
The historiography qualifier fits only one of four destinations; the others discuss revolution directly rather than its interpretation.

The heading combines food riots, political disturbances, urban and rural unrest, election violence, and different named local events. Subheads by cause, location, named event, and urban or rural setting would create useful access. Sixteen displays force readers to inspect unrelated disturbances to find a specific riot. The distinctions are separate events and causal types.

The heading combines Paris sections as administrative units, electoral assemblies, popular societies, military organizations, insurrectionary actors, and later targets of suppression. Subheads for administration, elections, popular politics, armed action, and suppression would provide useful routes. Twenty-six displays and forty-four assignments make a particular institutional function hard to retrieve. The divisions are distinct functions and historical phases.

The heading aggregates direct and indirect taxes, named levies, exemptions, collection, arrears, reform, protest, and wartime finance. Subheads by tax type, administration, reform, protest, and wartime use would provide essential access. Twenty-eight displays give no indication which tax or fiscal relationship each destination treats. The divisions are distinct fiscal instruments and processes.

The references concern trials of different defendants, political trials, institutional proceedings, and varying procedural or evidentiary issues. Subdivide by named defendant or case and by political versus institutional proceeding. Twenty-eight displays and thirty-two assignments leave readers to identify unrelated trials from page numbers alone. Cases and proceeding types are independent access concepts.

The references distinguish military policing, riot suppression, billeting, mutiny control, protection of institutions, and deployments by region or crisis. Subdivide by policing/riot control, billeting, mutiny, institutional protection, and major region or crisis. Thirty-seven displays and forty-six assignments make distinct domestic-order functions difficult to retrieve. The functions and situations are substantive, recurring concepts.

separate wars, coalitions, campaigns, theaters, and diplomatic phases. Useful routes: war—Austria and Prussia; Britain; coalition wars; theaters; diplomacy. Consequence: fifty-four displayed locators and long ranges make a targeted conflict or campaign difficult to retrieve.

critical_gates.description: systematic incidental or unsupported locator pattern
central subject or conclusion materially omitted
heading reverses or seriously misrepresents source stance
compound heading locators support only separate components
see source replaces a warranted substantive entry
unresolved, self-referential, circular, or chained cross-reference
systematic named-entity, example, or citation clutter
more than 1% of in-scope locator assignments uninspectable without a frozen alternative tolerance

comparison_key.inclusion_policy: Frozen current-V8 source scope and candidate-blind benchmark.
comparison_key.uncertainty_policy: Record uncertainty explicitly; adjudicate every critical, major, and uncertain item; exclude uninspectable locators from precision denominators and disclose them.

limitations: This evaluation covers the user-authorized derivative restricted to printed pages 1–425. The delivered index references beyond that common source scope were not evaluated.
The supplied source text matches the corresponding pages of the 2002 second edition. The exact file uploaded to the index producer was unavailable for byte-for-byte identity verification.

Density uses 194,718 indexable words from the exact imported source-discovery release. Historical chapter extraction methods vary; a separately authored evaluation uses a different word denominator and is not directly interchangeable.
